xetrader wrote: hi Amit, there a lot of topics, i am confused what to learn? do i have to learn all of these things? i like to stick with S/D with trend lines.. i have practiced on GBPAUD, and i think i am doing not very well but doing good, please tell me should i have to master myself on all topics here on RTM? thanks

When I was new, I also thought all the things are difficult to learn. But what i did is I learned these concepts separately then then tried to use them together.

1st understand what is supply and demand (SD). SD is not just where price dropped and raised. There are sub points of SD. like -Fresh (untested) SD, tested (visited 1 or more time) SD (we call it FTB, 2TB, 3TB...)... -Ignored SD, what happens when SD gets ignored, etc.

Take your time to understand the behaviour of price action with supply and demand. Then pick a 1 topic from marketpedia, lets say FTR. Then start learning and locating FTRs and observe how price behaves at these FTRs. Find the max information about FTR as possible as you can. Ask yourself why FTR occurred. Why price failed to return who failed. etc.

Then slowly slowly learn other topic and while learning them keep posting in home work. Watch videos by IF over and over again and notice what reasons he used to enter trade. Every week watch his all videos and read market pedia again and again and keep finding the concepts on your chart and observe how price behaves. This is a slow process but the more time and hardwork you will give to RTM, there more quickly you can learn. It does take time but you can learn it if you keep fighting with it. Read journals of Dr. Swing and Draft's journal. Very nice explanation is given for the entries. But before that learn the concepts separately one by one. Read trading article discussion thread.

وقتی تازه‌کار بودم، من هم فکر می‌کردم یادگیری همهٔ این چیزها سخت است. ولی کاری که کردم این بود که این مفاهیم را جدا یاد گرفتم و بعد سعی کردم با هم استفاده‌شان کنم.

اول بفهم عرضه و تقاضا (SD) چیست. SD فقط جایی نیست که قیمت افتاده و بالا رفته. زیرشاخه‌هایی دارد، مثل: عرضه/تقاضای تازه (تست‌نشده)، عرضه/تقاضای تست‌شده (1 بار یا بیشتر بازدیدشده) که به آن FTB، 2TB، 3TB... می‌گوییم... عرضه/تقاضای نادیده‌گرفته‌شده، و اینکه وقتی SD نادیده گرفته می‌شود چه اتفاقی می‌افتد، و غیره.

وقت بگذار تا رفتار پرایس اکشن را همراه عرضه و تقاضا بفهمی. بعد یک موضوع از Marketpedia انتخاب کن، مثلاً FTR. آن‌گاه شروع کن به یادگیری و پیدا کردن FTR‌ها و ببین قیمت در این FTR‌ها چطور رفتار می‌کند. تا می‌توانی بیشترین اطلاعات را دربارهٔ FTR جمع کن. از خودت بپرس چرا FTR رخ داد. چرا قیمت برنگشت، چه کسی شکست خورد. و غیره.

بعد آهسته‌آهسته موضوع‌های دیگر را یاد بگیر و همان موقع یادگیری، در بخش تکلیف پست بگذار. ویدئوهای IF را بارها و بارها ببین و توجه کن از چه دلایلی برای ورود استفاده کرده. هر هفته همهٔ ویدئوهایش را ببین و Marketpedia را دوباره و دوباره بخوان و مدام مفاهیم را روی چارتت پیدا کن و ببین قیمت چطور رفتار می‌کند. این فرایند کندی است، ولی هر چه وقت و تلاش بیشتری به RTM بدهی، سریع‌تر یاد می‌گیری. زمان می‌برد، ولی اگر مدام با آن بجنگی یاد می‌گیری. ژورنال Dr. Swing و ژورنال Draft را بخوان. برای ورودها توضیح خیلی خوبی داده شده. ولی قبل از آن، مفاهیم را یکی‌یکی و جدا یاد بگیر. تردِ بحثِ مقالهٔ معامله‌گری را بخوان.

Option A: Enter when price hits the lower edge of the black box. Price doesn't hit SL, exit at blue box. R:R approx 1:1.5 Option B: Hold off on entering as in option A and instead see if price makes a deeper retrace. It does, enter at the lower edge of the red box. Risking 2% on option A you have made 3% Risking 2% on option B you have made 30%

Following option B will cause you to miss trades, following option A will cause you to enter every trade. There can be a lot of comfort in trading one particular lot size, day in, day out.

But, if the trade we're in now demands a stop twice as far as the last trade needed, then really we should halve our position size. If it only needs half the space, then our plan should have us doubling the position size. If we're up 10% from our last trade, and our next trade needs the same stop distance, we should be trading 110% of the last position, so we can compound.

Ok, Suppose, you are a shopkeeper and you want to sell your product (You want to make a Transaction) but there is no any customer visiting your shop because your shop is at a lonely place.

So, here, what would you do? You would put your shop at the place where there is too much rush of people. i.e where people can make transactions. Those places can be a Street where many people walk everyday or a marketplace where people go to buy their daily needed products. Same as if you want to catch fish, you have to go to the river. River doesn't come to your home. right?

So, here you found "The places where most of the Transactions happens."

The same way, there are specific levels where transactions happens i.e. IT as a Shopkeeper and Retailers are Customers. And those places are where IT can play their tricks because at those levels there is too much rush of retail traders. (People's favorite places / Usual places where they jump into market or out of the market). These levels are like a Marketplace.

So, what you need to know (most of you already know) that the places where People like to trade and because of that IT get chance to play tricks with them.

So, these places (Market places) are:

Support and resistance (horizontal) Support and resistance (Trendline) (I don't use trendline though) Supply and Demand levels Round Numbers (Many times) Important News events Top of the Range Market Bottom of the Range Market Breakout of specific levels. Their stop losses are at nearest high or low.

In my opinion above are the places where IT likes to play with emotions of retailers by tricks with them.

No matter what TF you see. HTF, LTF is like Long term and Short term thing. You need to read the price action story left to right. Price moves from one place to another by consuming orders. You need to see how the orders are consumed and what happens when price comes back to that consumption. If it reacts there then you need to look more back history to know why it reacted there and if not reacted even that you need to look back to know why it didn't reacted. Draw horizontal lines on swing high and low and look left for the reason and see if the reason is repeated. Keep in mind about the consumption, decision and PA story.

Consumption and decision is one of the major cause of price movement. You need to see IF's all videos (again and again) to know how to read price story. Follow the Risk Reward ratio rule. Never break you own rules and discipline. Have a patience. I use at least min 1:8 R:R ratio. Observation is more powerful thing than doing practice. I found many clues by observing than practice trading.

You need to know the psychological reasons for the drop and rise of the prices after formation of the flag. Rally-base-Drop has a base which is also a flag. When price consolidate in a side ways within a range for a while and breaks one of the sides some times both the sides by faking out then you need to visualize what happened behind the charts. People look left to see where it reacted but forgets to look left of the left.

1] For me there is no specific and only single reason for the formation of important high (or low). And the things is that each and every high and low is important according to their respective TFs.Here the TFs means the terms, short term, long term, medium term. You should have eye on the these SDs and should watch and IMAGINE what ITs are trying to do at these levels. Then you can see the decision. Ask yourself who bought, who sold around the highs/lows, SDs etc and who failed how & why. If they failed then where the extreme limit of their failure. It can be a decision point as well as QM if price FO.

2] Targets can be the origin of the move. See the beginning posts of FF RTM thread.

3] Video about CAPs by IF is very good to know about how to draw the boxes.
